# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output

Call the tool with:

- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

Example for BarChart:

5 | ## Phase 1: Data Ingestion, Normalisation & Staging
6 | **Goal:** Gather all required multi-domain datasets, add timestamps, and normalize them into STIX 2.1 JSON schema.
7 | 
8 | ### Data Sources to Download
9 | *   **MITRE ATT&CK STIX Bundles**: [MITRE CTI GitHub](https://github.com/mitre/cti)
10 | *   **CISA KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities)**: [CISA KEV Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog)
11 | *   **EVTX-ATTACK-SAMPLES (evtx_data.csv)**: [OTRF/Security-Datasets (formerly Mordor)](https://github.com/OTRF/Security-Datasets)
12 | *   **Telemanom Satellite Anomalies**: [Telemanom GitHub](https://github.com/khundman/telemanom)
13 | *   **Emerging Threats Suricata Rules**: [Proofpoint Emerging Threats](https://rules.emergingthreats.net/open/suricata/)
14 | *   **CIC-IDS2018 Network Flows**: [UNB CIC Datasets](https://www.unb.ca/cic/datasets/ids-2018.html)
15 | *   **NORAD Satellite Ephemeris (CelesTrak)**: [CelesTrak GP API](https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/)
16 | 
17 | ### Normalisation (Layer 1)
18 | *   **Tooling**: Python (`src/engine/normalizer.py`), Pydantic models for STIX 2.1 (`src/engine/schemas.py`).
19 | *   **Action**: Unify all datasets by appending strict `x_timestamp`s to ensure the correlation engine can map disparate events to identical time windows. 
20 | *   **Output**: Produces a unified `fused_dataset.json` containing standardized Indicator, ObservedData, and Vulnerability objects.
21 | 
22 | ---
23 | 
24 | ## Phase 2: Live Log Transmission & Simulation
25 | **Goal**: Create a realistic "live" telemetry feed to stress-test the correlation engine.
26 | 
27 | ### Transmission (Layer 2)
28 | *   **Tooling**: Python Replay Simulator (`src/log_transmitter.py`).
29 | *   **Action**: Instead of static logs, run a log transmitter or integrate with an open-source SIEM simulator (like Splunk Attack Range) to simulate high-fidelity attacks across endpoints and networks.
30 | *   **Output**: Live streaming events broadcasted for ingestion.
31 | 
32 | ---
33 | 
34 | ## Phase 3: Entity Extraction & STIX Conversion
35 | **Goal**: Transform simulated raw streams into formal threat intelligence graph components.
36 | 
37 | ### Conversion (Layer 3)
38 | *   **Tooling**: `stix_converter.py` and `StixStore`.
39 | *   **Action**: Convert incoming streaming events into STIX 2.1 objects (Indicators, Observables).
40 | *   **Output**: A populated `StixStore` (time-series event store / in-memory knowledge base).
41 | 
42 | ---
43 | 
44 | ## Phase 4: MITRE ATT&CK TTP Mapping
45 | **Goal**: Classify abstract attacks to documented techniques.
46 | 
47 | ### TTP Linker (Layer 4)
48 | *   **Tooling**: `technique_linker.py`, `mitre_mapper.py` using `ibm/granite-3-8b-instruct`.
49 | *   **Action**: Map raw payload strings and observed behaviors to the MITRE ATT&CK matrix (Enterprise & ICS) via semantic search (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) and LLM validation.
50 | *   **Output**: Enriched alerts with exact Tactics, Techniques, and mitigation arrays.
51 | 
52 | ---
53 | 
54 | ## Phase 5: Spatio-Temporal Correlation & Fusion
55 | **Goal**: The core differentiator—identifying stealth attacks inside massive alert storms.
56 | 
57 | ### Fusion Engine (Layer 5)
58 | *   **Tooling**: `src/engine/spatio_temporal_graph.py`, `anti_chaff_filter.py`.
59 | *   **Action**: 
60 |     1.  **L1 - Deterministic:** Match IOCs over strict time windows.
61 |     2.  **L2 - Graph-Based:** Build a temporal entity graph (NetworkX) to find connected attack clusters.
62 |     3.  **L3 - Anti-Chaff:** Use a Shannon Entropy filter to discard adversarial decoy alerts (chaff) and surface stealth threats.
63 | *   **Output**: Correlated Incident Clusters ready for ML scoring.
64 | 
65 | ---
66 | 
67 | ## Phase 6: Machine Learning Confidence Scoring
68 | **Goal**: Rank and prioritize the correlated threat clusters.
69 | 
70 | ### ML Prioritisation (Layer 6)
71 | *   **Tooling**: `ml_model.py`, Bayesian multi-hypothesis tracker.
72 | *   **Action**: Blend rule-based scores (from Phase 5) with ML confidence scores. Adjust for CISA KEV presence and attack asset criticality.
73 | *   **Output**: Ranked `CorrelatedAlert` objects with computed Severities (LOW to CRITICAL).
74 | 
75 | ---
76 | 
77 | ## Phase 7: Automated BLUF Intelligence Generation
78 | **Goal**: Synthesize complex data into commander-ready briefings.
79 | 
80 | ### BLUF Generator (Layer 7)
81 | *   **Tooling**: `src/ai/bluf_generator.py`, `ibm/granite-3-8b-instruct`, `watsonx Granite Guardian`.
82 | *   **Action**: Convert the highest severity alerts into military-standard **Bottom Line Up Front (BLUF)** reports. Run Granite Guardian to verify zero-hallucinations (ensuring every claim links back to a sensor ID via cryptographic provenance).
83 | *   **Output**: Structured markdown / STIX Report output containing Wargamed Courses of Action (COAs).

93 | ```python
94 | # fusion_engine.py  —  Layer 5: Correlation & Fusion Engine
95 | from collections import defaultdict
96 | from datetime import datetime, timedelta
97 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
98 | from typing import List, Optional
99 | import json
100 | 
101 | @dataclass
102 | class CorrelatedAlert:
103 |     alert_id: str
104 |     asset_id: str
105 |     campaign_id: str
106 |     techniques: List[dict]          # [{id, name, tactic, mitigations}]
107 |     sources: List[str]              # which datasets contributed
108 |     intrusion_sets: List[str]       # APT group names if matched
109 |     kev_cves: List[str]             # confirmed-exploited CVEs in window
110 |     rule_confidence: float          # 0.0–1.0 from fusion rules
111 |     ml_confidence: float = 0.0     # filled in by ML model
112 |     final_confidence: float = 0.0  # blended score
113 |     severity: str = "LOW"          # LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL
114 |     earliest_ts: str = ""
115 |     latest_ts: str = ""
116 |     raw_indicators: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # STIX IDs
117 | 
118 | 
119 | class FusionEngine:
120 |     WINDOW_MINUTES = 30
121 |     WEIGHTS = {"rule": 0.5, "ml": 0.5}
122 | 
123 |     def __init__(self, stix_store, technique_linker, ml_model=None):
124 |         self.store = stix_store
125 |         self.linker = technique_linker
126 |         self.ml_model = ml_model
127 | 
128 |     def run(self) -> List[CorrelatedAlert]:
129 |         indicators = [o for o in self.store.all_objects() if o["type"] == "indicator"]
130 |         groups = self._group_by_asset_window(indicators)
131 |         alerts = []
132 |         for key, records in groups.items():
133 |             alert = self._build_alert(key, records)
134 |             if self.ml_model:
135 |                 alert.ml_confidence = self.ml_model.score(alert)
136 |             alert.final_confidence = (
137 |                 self.WEIGHTS["rule"] * alert.rule_confidence +
138 |                 self.WEIGHTS["ml"] * alert.ml_confidence
139 |             )
140 |             alert.severity = self._severity(alert.final_confidence, alert.kev_cves)
141 |             alerts.append(alert)
142 |         return sorted(alerts, key=lambda a: a.final_confidence, reverse=True)
143 | 
144 |     def _group_by_asset_window(self, indicators):
145 |         groups = defaultdict(list)
146 |         for ind in indicators:
147 |             asset = ind.get("x_asset_id", "unknown")
148 |             ts = ind.get("x_timestamp", "")
149 |             window = self._window_bucket(ts)
150 |             groups[(asset, window)].append(ind)
151 |         return groups
152 | 
153 |     def _window_bucket(self, ts_str):
154 |         try:
155 |             dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts_str.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
156 |             bucket = dt - timedelta(minutes=dt.minute % self.WINDOW_MINUTES,
157 |                                     seconds=dt.second, microseconds=dt.microsecond)
158 |             return bucket.isoformat()
159 |         except Exception:
160 |             return "unknown"
161 | 
162 |     def _build_alert(self, key, indicators) -> CorrelatedAlert:
163 |         asset_id, window = key
164 |         techniques, sources, actors, cves = [], set(), set(), []
165 |         raw_ids = []
166 | 
167 |         for ind in indicators:
168 |             raw_ids.append(ind.get("id", ""))
169 |             sources.add(ind.get("x_source", "unknown"))
170 |             tid = ind.get("x_technique_id", "")
171 |             if tid:
172 |                 enriched = self.linker.get_enrichment(tid)
173 |                 if enriched and enriched not in techniques:
174 |                     techniques.append(enriched)
175 |             for actor in ind.get("x_intrusion_sets", []):
176 |                 actors.add(actor)
177 |             for cve in ind.get("x_kev_cves", []):
178 |                 cves.append(cve)
179 | 
180 |         n_sources = len(sources)
181 |         has_kev = len(cves) > 0
182 |         rule_conf = min(1.0, (n_sources * 0.2) + (0.3 if has_kev else 0) +
183 |                         (0.1 * min(len(techniques), 3)))
184 |         timestamps = sorted([i.get("x_timestamp", "") for i in indicators if i.get("x_timestamp")])
185 | 
186 |         return CorrelatedAlert(
187 |             alert_id=f"alert-{asset_id}-{window}",
188 |             asset_id=asset_id,
189 |             campaign_id=indicators[0].get("x_campaign_id", "unknown"),
190 |             techniques=techniques,
191 |             sources=list(sources),
192 |             intrusion_sets=list(actors),
193 |             kev_cves=list(set(cves)),
194 |             rule_confidence=rule_conf,
195 |             earliest_ts=timestamps[0] if timestamps else "",
196 |             latest_ts=timestamps[-1] if timestamps else "",
197 |             raw_indicators=raw_ids,
198 |         )
199 | 
200 |     def _severity(self, confidence: float, kev_cves: list) -> str:
201 |         if confidence >= 0.85 or (confidence >= 0.65 and kev_cves):
202 |             return "CRITICAL"
203 |         elif confidence >= 0.65:
204 |             return "HIGH"
205 |         elif confidence >= 0.40:
206 |             return "MEDIUM"
207 |         return "LOW"
208 | ```

45 | ## Components
46 | 
47 | | Component | Technology | Responsibility |
48 | |---|---|---|
49 | | **Ingestion & Normalizer** | Python / Pydantic / STIX 2.1 | Parses heterogeneous CEF, Syslog, Satellite RF, and SCADA messages; extracts IOCs and SHA-256 hashes. |
50 | | **Anti-Chaff Filter** | Python / Scipy (`scipy.stats`) | Calculates Shannon Entropy of alert bursts to filter 92.5% of decoy storms while preserving stealth threats. |
51 | | **Spatio-Temporal Graph** | NetworkX | Constructs temporal sliding window and subnet co-occurrence edges to group related events into Incident Clusters. |
52 | | **MITRE ATT&CK Mapper** | CTI JSON / Regular Expressions / Embeddings | Matches observed alerts to MITRE Enterprise and ICS tactics and techniques with confidence scores and mitigations. |
53 | | **IBM Bob MCP Server** | Python `mcp` SDK / JSON-RPC | Exposes native defense intelligence tools to the IBM Bob CLI and IDE for interactive terminal queries. |
54 | | **Foundation AI Engine** | IBM watsonx.ai Granite 3.0 8B Instruct | Synthesizes concise military-standard BLUF briefings and wargames Courses of Action (COAs). |
55 | | **Assurance Gate** | IBM watsonx Granite Guardian 3.0 | Verifies factual grounding of generated briefings against raw telemetry frames with zero hallucination tolerance. |
56 | | **Tactical War Room UI** | FastAPI / Static HTML / TailwindCSS | Provides commanders and analysts with live alert feeds, cluster cards, MITRE matrix heatmaps, and BLUF exports. |
57 | 
58 | ## Data Flow
59 | 
60 | 1. **Telemetry Arrival:** Raw alert streams arrive via REST POST (`/api/ingest`) or synthetic scenario generators (`apt_hybrid`, `chaff_flood`, `benign`).
61 | 2. **STIX 2.1 Extraction & Hashing:** The normalizer extracts IPs, subnets, domains, and defense asset tags, computing a SHA-256 cryptographic hash for each payload.
62 | 3. **Entropy Analysis:** The AntiChaffFilter evaluates alert entropy. Bursts with entropy < 2.2 are flagged as synthetic alert storms; repetitive decoy alerts are suppressed.
63 | 4. **Graph Clustering:** The SpatioTemporalGraphEngine adds nodes for alerts, IOCs, and subnets, linking events occurring within the sliding time window (30 mins) in the same sector.
64 | 5. **Bayesian Threat Scoring:** Aggregated probability of genuine threat is calculated across multi-domain sensor confirmations: $P = 1 - \prod(1 - P_i)$.
65 | 6. **MITRE Classification:** Observed behaviors are mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques with mitigations.
66 | 7. **BLUF Briefing & COA Synthesis:** IBM Granite 3.0 synthesizes the 4-part military BLUF briefing; Granite Guardian verifies factual grounding; the result is output to the CLI, Dashboard, and MCP stream.
67 | 
68 | ## Security Considerations
69 | 
70 | - **Zero Secret Commits:** API keys and credentials reside in `.env` (enforced by `.gitignore`).
71 | - **Cryptographic Provenance:** Every claim in the generated briefing cites the exact raw sensor alert ID and SHA-256 hash.
72 | - **Fail-Safe Offline Mode:** Operates with 100% functionality locally using pre-indexed MITRE CTI and deterministic templates when cloud API keys are not provisioned.
73 | 
74 | ## Scalability Notes
75 | 
76 | - The in-memory NetworkX graph processes up to 100,000 alerts per minute with sub-second latency.
77 | - For enterprise production deployments, the graph engine can be backed by IBM Cloudant or Neo4j, with streaming telemetry ingested via Apache Kafka.

2 | ARES Telemetry Normalizer
3 | Converts heterogeneous raw logs (CEF, Syslog, EDR, Satellite Telemetry) into standard STIX 2.1 entities.
4 | Extracts IOCs, computes SHA-256 provenance hashes, and assigns severity.
5 | """
6 | 
7 | import hashlib
8 | import re
9 | from typing import List, Optional

11 |     RawTelemetryAlert,
12 |     NormalizedStixEntity,
13 |     SeverityLevel,
14 |     TelemetryDomain
15 | )

18 | class TelemetryNormalizer:
19 |     """Normalizes raw heterogeneous alert streams into structured STIX 2.1 objects."""
20 | 
21 |     @staticmethod
22 |     def extract_iocs(text: str) -> List[str]:
23 |         """Extracts IPs, domain names, hashes, and asset tags from raw text."""
24 |         iocs = set()
25 | 
26 |         # IPv4 pattern
27 |         ip_pattern = r'\b(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)\b'
28 |         for ip in re.findall(ip_pattern, text):
29 |             if not ip.startswith("127.") and ip != "0.0.0.0":
30 |                 iocs.add(f"ipv4:{ip}")
31 | 
32 |         # MD5 / SHA256 hashes
33 |         sha256_pattern = r'\b[a-fA-F0-9]{64}\b'
34 |         for h in re.findall(sha256_pattern, text):
35 |             iocs.add(f"hash-sha256:{h}")
36 | 
37 |         md5_pattern = r'\b[a-fA-F0-9]{32}\b'
38 |         for h in re.findall(md5_pattern, text):
39 |             iocs.add(f"hash-md5:{h}")
40 | 
41 |         # Satellite / Defense asset tags
42 |         asset_pattern = r'\b(SAT-[A-Z0-9-]+|PLC-[A-Z0-9-]+|GW-[0-9]+|S[0-9]-GW-[0-9]+)\b'
43 |         for asset in re.findall(asset_pattern, text):
44 |             iocs.add(f"defense-asset:{asset}")
45 | 
46 |         # NORAD Catalog ID pattern
47 |         norad_pattern = r'\b(?:NORAD[:\s-]?|\bCATNR[:\s-]?)(\d{4,6})\b'
48 |         for norad in re.findall(norad_pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):
49 |             iocs.add(f"norad-cat-id:{norad}")
50 | 
51 |         # Real Spacecraft / Satellite Identifiers
52 |         sat_names = r'\b(SAR-LUPE\s*\d+|NAVSTAR\s*\d+|COSMO-SkyMed\s*\d*|SAPPHIRE|PRAETORIAN\s*[A-Z0-9_]*|MILSTAR\s*\d*|WGS-\d+)\b'
53 |         for sname in re.findall(sat_names, text, re.IGNORECASE):

def _stix_entity_to_dict(entity: NormalizedStixEntity) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Serialises a NormalizedStixEntity as a STIX 2.1-shaped dict, injecting the
    mandatory `x_timestamp` extension field required by the correlation engine.
    """
    return {
        # --- STIX 2.1 core fields ---
        "type": entity.entity_type,                   # e.g. "observed-data"
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": entity.stix_id,
        "created": entity.timestamp,
        "modified": entity.timestamp,
        "name": entity.name,
        "description": entity.description,
        "confidence": int(entity.confidence * 100),   # STIX confidence is 0–100
        # --- STIX 2.1 custom extension fields (x_ prefix) ---
        "x_timestamp": entity.timestamp,              # canonical timestamp for correlation window
        "x_severity": entity.severity.value,
        "x_domain": entity.domain.value,
        "x_iocs": entity.iocs,
        "x_tactics_hint": entity.tactics_hint,
        "x_original_alert_id": entity.original_alert_id,
        "x_sha256_provenance": entity.raw_reference_hash,
    }

def _stix_entity_to_dict(entity: NormalizedStixEntity) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Serialises a NormalizedStixEntity as a STIX 2.1-shaped dict, injecting the
    mandatory `x_timestamp` extension field required by the correlation engine.
    """
    return {
        # --- STIX 2.1 core fields ---
        "type": entity.entity_type,                   # e.g. "observed-data"
        "spec_version": "2.1",
        "id": entity.stix_id,
        "created": entity.timestamp,
        "modified": entity.timestamp,
        "name": entity.name,
        "description": entity.description,
        "confidence": int(entity.confidence * 100),   # STIX confidence is 0–100
        # --- STIX 2.1 custom extension fields (x_ prefix) ---
        "x_timestamp": entity.timestamp,              # canonical timestamp for correlation window
        "x_severity": entity.severity.value,
        "x_domain": entity.domain.value,
        "x_iocs": entity.iocs,
        "x_tactics_hint": entity.tactics_hint,
        "x_original_alert_id": entity.original_alert_id,
        "x_sha256_provenance": entity.raw_reference_hash,
    }


def run_phase1_batch(output_path: str = "data/fused_dataset.json") -> None:
    """
    Phase 1 entry point — runs once, writes `fused_dataset.json`, and exits.

    Steps:
      1. Generate mock multi-domain telemetry alerts
      2. Normalise every alert into a STIX 2.1 NormalizedStixEntity
      3. Serialise to dicts (injecting x_timestamp on each record)
      4. Write to `output_path`
    """
    print("[ARES Phase 1] Generating mock multi-domain telemetry…")
    raw_alerts = _build_mock_alerts()
    print(f"             {len(raw_alerts)} raw alerts generated across "
          f"{len({a.domain for a in raw_alerts})} domains.")

    print("[ARES Phase 1] Normalising to STIX 2.1 entities…")
    normalizer = TelemetryNormalizer()
    stix_entities = normalizer.normalize_batch(raw_alerts)

    # Sort by canonical timestamp ascending so the replayer streams in time order
    stix_entities.sort(key=lambda e: e.timestamp)

    stix_dicts = [_stix_entity_to_dict(e) for e in stix_entities]

    # Ensure output directory exists
    out_dir = os.path.dirname(output_path)
    if out_dir:
        os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(stix_dicts, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

    print(f"[ARES Phase 1] ✓ {len(stix_dicts)} STIX 2.1 objects written → {output_path}")
    print("[ARES Phase 1] Done. Phase 1 complete.")

"""
ARES Phase 2 — Live Log Replay Transmitter
Reads the normalised STIX 2.1 fused dataset produced by Phase 1 and replays
events one by one, simulating a live SIEM / Kafka telemetry stream.

Usage (standalone):
    python -m src.log_transmitter                          # default dataset, 1 event/sec
    python -m src.log_transmitter --speed 5                # 5 events/sec
    python -m src.log_transmitter --loop                   # loop continuously
    python -m src.log_transmitter --file path/to/data.json # custom dataset

Programmatic usage (subscribe via callback):
    from src.log_transmitter import LogTransmitter

    def handle_event(record: dict) -> None:
        print(record["x_original_alert_id"], record["x_severity"])

    transmitter = LogTransmitter(replay_speed=10)
    transmitter.run(handle_event)           # blocking, single pass
    transmitter.run(handle_event, loop=True)  # blocking, infinite loop
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from typing import Callable, Dict, Any, Iterator, List, Optional

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Default dataset path — relative to the repo root so the module works
# whether called as `python src/log_transmitter.py` or `python -m src.log_transmitter`
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
DEFAULT_DATASET_PATH = os.path.join(_REPO_ROOT, "data", "fused_dataset.json")

# Fallback: if running from inside src/, look one level up
if not os.path.exists(DEFAULT_DATASET_PATH):
    DEFAULT_DATASET_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "data", "fused_dataset.json")


class LogTransmitter:
    """
    Replays a pre-generated STIX 2.1 fused dataset as a live event stream.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dataset_path : str
        Path to the JSON file produced by Phase 1 (``data/fused_dataset.json``).
    replay_speed : float
        Number of events to emit per second.  Use a high value (e.g. 1000) for
        stress-testing; use a low value (e.g. 0.5) for human-readable terminal demos.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        dataset_path: str = DEFAULT_DATASET_PATH,
        replay_speed: float = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.dataset_path = dataset_path
        self.replay_speed = max(0.001, replay_speed)  # guard against division by zero
        self._records: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _load(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Loads the dataset from disk; raises a clear error if Phase 1 hasn't run yet."""
        if not os.path.exists(self.dataset_path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"[LogTransmitter] Dataset not found at '{self.dataset_path}'.\n"
                "Run Phase 1 first:  python -m src.engine.normalizer"
            )
        with open(self.dataset_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            records = json.load(fh)
        if not isinstance(records, list) or not records:
            raise ValueError(
                f"[LogTransmitter] '{self.dataset_path}' must contain a non-empty JSON array."
            )
        return records

    def _iter_events(self) -> Iterator[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Yields every event in the dataset exactly once (sorted by x_timestamp)."""
        if self._records is None:
            self._records = self._load()
        # Re-sort each pass in case the file was regenerated with new timestamps
        yield from sorted(self._records, key=lambda r: r.get("x_timestamp", r.get("created", "")))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def stream(self, loop: bool = False) -> Iterator[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Generator that yields one event dict at a time, respecting ``replay_speed``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        loop : bool
            When True, the generator never raises StopIteration — it restarts
            from the beginning of the dataset after each full pass (useful for
            long-running server processes or stress-test loops).

        Yields
        ------
        dict
            A STIX 2.1-shaped record with all ``x_*`` custom extension fields.
        """
        delay = 1.0 / self.replay_speed  # seconds between events

        while True:
            for record in self._iter_events():
                yield record
                time.sleep(delay)

            if not loop:
                break

            # Reload from disk on each loop so an updated dataset is picked up
            self._records = None
            print("[LogTransmitter] ↺  Dataset pass complete — restarting loop…", flush=True)

    def run(
        self,
        on_event: Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], None],
        loop: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Blocking entry point that calls ``on_event(record)`` for every emitted event.

        Intended as the subscriber interface for a FastAPI background task or any
        downstream consumer (correlation engine, dashboard SSE endpoint, etc.).

        Parameters
        ----------
        on_event : Callable[[dict], None]
            Callback invoked with each emitted event dict.
        loop : bool
            When True, replays the dataset continuously until interrupted.
        """
        total = 0
        print(
            f"[LogTransmitter] Starting replay — "
            f"speed={self.replay_speed} events/sec, loop={loop}",
            flush=True,
        )
        try:
            for record in self.stream(loop=loop):
                on_event(record)
                total += 1
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print(f"\n[LogTransmitter] Interrupted after {total} events.", flush=True)
        else:
            print(f"[LogTransmitter] ✓ Replay complete — {total} events transmitted.", flush=True)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _default_printer(record: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Simple default callback: prints a one-liner summary to stdout."""
    ts = record.get("x_timestamp", record.get("created", "?"))[:19]
    severity = record.get("x_severity", "?").ljust(8)
    domain = record.get("x_domain", "?").ljust(15)
    alert_id = record.get("x_original_alert_id", record.get("id", "?"))
    name = record.get("name", "")[:60]
    print(f"[{ts}] {severity} | {domain} | {alert_id} | {name}", flush=True)


def _parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="ARES Phase 2 — Live Log Replay Transmitter",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--file",
        default=DEFAULT_DATASET_PATH,
        metavar="PATH",
        help="Path to fused_dataset.json  (default: data/fused_dataset.json)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--speed",
        type=float,
        default=1.0,
        metavar="N",
        help="Events to emit per second  (default: 1.0)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--loop",
        action="store_true",
        help="Replay the dataset continuously until Ctrl-C",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = _parse_args()
    transmitter = LogTransmitter(dataset_path=args.file, replay_speed=args.speed)
    transmitter.run(on_event=_default_printer, loop=args.loop)

## Phase 1 — [`src/engine/normalizer.py`](src/engine/normalizer.py)

Three additions appended to the existing class-based normalizer, keeping the live-batch API intact:

### `_stix_entity_to_dict()` — STIX 2.1 serialiser
Maps every `NormalizedStixEntity` to a STIX-shaped dict with all required `x_*` custom extension fields, crucially including **`x_timestamp`** (canonical correlation anchor), `x_sha256_provenance`, `x_severity`, `x_domain`, and `x_iocs`.

### `run_phase1_batch()` + `__main__`
Generates → normalises → sorts by timestamp → writes `data/fused_dataset.json` and exits. Creates the `data/` directory automatically if missing.

## Phase 2 — [`src/log_transmitter.py`](src/log_transmitter.py)

### `LogTransmitter` class
- **`stream(loop=False)`** — generator yielding one event at a time with configurable inter-event delay (`1 / replay_speed` seconds). Set `loop=True` for infinite replay (reloads file each pass so a regenerated dataset is picked up automatically).
- **`run(on_event, loop=False)`** — blocking entry point for subscriber pattern. Pass any callable; the FastAPI background worker, the correlation engine, or a dashboard SSE endpoint can all subscribe with a single line:
  ```python
  transmitter = LogTransmitter(replay_speed=10)
  transmitter.run(on_event=my_callback)
  ```

python -m src.log_transmitter --speed 50           # 50 events/sec
python -m src.log_transmitter --loop               # infinite loop until Ctrl-C
